differences.what: Turntable is larger in frame and evenly lit; the red acrylic plinth reads as glowing, clear material with a clean edge line, while in B the lower plinth and arm board sink into a murky magenta-red with little edge definition
B has a cropped speaker cabinet at the left edge with a hot magenta-violet glow and bright vertical light panels that pull the eye off the product; A's left side is clean wall and cabinet
B's red-magenta colour cast drowns the walnut and turns the record and tonearm muddy; A holds a warm but more neutral grade where the walnut grain and black arm separate from the red acrylic
B's plaster wall carries a denoiser smear and painterly blotches, plus a dark speck at top left; A's wall is smoother, with less visible artifacting
Tonearm, counterweight and arm rest are crisper with better form shading in B; in A they are soft and slightly blurred at 3x

B's lower camera, wall shadow and moodier light give more depth and atmosphere; A's flat frontal warm light reads as a flatter catalogue shot, with too much slatted cabinet front taking the bottom third
A's lamp is cut by the top frame edge and its shade is big enough to compete with the turntable; in B it is smaller and balanced against the speaker
